**📝 REVIEW: MDX23C-8KFFT-InstVoc_HQ — the program that did this removal.** Every claim below is from our own measurements across this project. Fair means both directions.

**Scorecard**

| dimension | grade | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Loud/direct voice removal | **A** | this track: −51.1 dB in the recognizability band, statistically tied with the best transformer (roformer −52.7) |
| Orchestra preservation | **A−** | transparent where no voice (removal print −17.4 dB, ~5 dB *below* the orchestra's own level); keeps brightness roformer destroys (verdi_slow air −11.6 vs −19.4 dB) |
| Quiet voice under loud orchestra | **D** | Scary_Dog soprano: −31.6 dB removal vs roformer's −49.6 — an 18 dB gap, audibly leaked, lost the track; the same blindness missed quiet reverberant voice in our cross-corpus tests |
| Its vocals stem (the other output) | **F** | stems do not sum to the mix (residual peaks 0.84 full-scale); subtraction variants built from it were the dirtiest on every single track (detector 0.86 vs 0.50); its stem under-reports exactly the voices its instrumental leaks — using it as a guide once routed our splice to the leakiest model (the circular-router failure) |
| Consistency / predictability | **C** | brilliant on this Verdi, beaten by 18 dB on the Stabat soprano — nothing in the material predicts which you will get; every track must be measured |
| Honesty about failure | **F** | no confidence signal of any kind: it fails silently, at full quality-of-output confidence — the entire human listening gate of this project exists because of this |
| Speed / robustness | **A** | seconds per track on one GPU; float-clean; unbothered by a hot master (1.84 float peaks) |

**In praise:** on direct, well-recorded voices it is a remarkable instrument — surgical (13 dB hotter removal in sung frames than silent ones), formant-accurate, and it leaves the orchestra its air. As a *default first pass* it earned its place.

**Without mercy:** it is deaf exactly where opera lives — the quiet phrase under the swell, the reverberant tail — and it will not tell you. Its vocal stem is not a measurement, it is an opinion, and trusting that opinion anywhere near a routing or QA decision produces confidently wrong systems. Ship nothing it touches without independent ears or an independent meter.

**Verdict: a tool to trust to *try* — never to *certify*.** Use it first, measure it always, and keep roformer loaded for the voices it cannot hear.

How do we do takeover? What is the blending boundary algo? And finally, do we recover crispness as learned where there is no voice?

Three good questions — exact answers:

**1. How the takeover works.** Both A and C are *full-length* renders of the same master, sample-aligned by construction. F is a pure time-domain mix: at every sample, `out(t) = w(t)·C(t) + (1−w(t))·A(t)` with w between 0 and 1. Full-band — no frequency splitting (we tried a frequency blend on Scary_Dog: taking A's highs re-imported the soprano's formants; rejected).

**2. The boundary algorithm.**
- *Router signal:* the independent voice detector (a small neural net trained on 466 opera voice/orchestra pairs — no relation to either separator) listening to **A's output**, probability per 10 ms, median-smoothed over ~0.5 s.
- *Decision:* hysteresis — enter a C-region when P > 0.55, return to A only when P < 0.45 (the double threshold prevents flutter); regions shorter than 0.6 s dropped, gaps under 1.0 s merged (so her breaths inside a phrase do NOT flip back to A); final regions padded ±0.25 s.
- *Blend shape:* the 0/1 gate is smoothed with a 150 ms moving average → linear amplitude-complementary ramps. Amplitude- (not power-) complementary is deliberate: A and C are highly **coherent** (same master, both mostly orchestra), and for coherent signals equal-gain sums preserve level — an equal-power ramp would bump ~+3 dB at every seam.
- *Result on this track:* C owns 6.3–7.1 s, 9.1–10.3 s, 20.0–42.7 s; A owns the rest (50%).

**3. Crispness where there is no voice — yes, but only in A-regions.** Where the router leaves A in charge, you get A, and A is measured near-transparent when nobody sings (on the verdi material: −0.3 dB himid, −0.7 presence, −1.8 air vs the original). Inside the C-regions the crispness is **not** recovered — C's dullness rules there, including through her short rests within 20–42.7 s (hysteresis deliberately holds C through them, safety over sparkle). The learned restorer (hole-filler v1) is NOT applied here: it was trained on mdx23c damage and we measured it unable to undo roformer's gouging (C+fill ≈ C). The honest path to crisp-inside-the-sung-region is training a **hole-filler v2 on roformer-damaged pairs** — a literature-backed GPU run I can start on your word. Until then, dull-where-she-sings is the price of voice-free.
